answer: The sable wharf exchange enforces work admission: each earning key must solve 20 fresh private constraint puzzles, and a verifier rejects incomplete batches before rewards unlock. Assignments bind to that key; disjoint puzzle sets prevent one solved batch enrolling many aliases. The marble desk records used assignments to stop replay. Every extra alias needs another batch of work. Generating and checking puzzles must be cheaper than solving them; faster solvers still gain an advantage.
